budget.latex: \begin{aligned} &\max\left\{ 2048 \cdot \left(\frac{\sigma^{2}}{I \cdot \varepsilon} + A \cdot \left(1 + \log\left(1 + \frac{R^{2}}{\varepsilon}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(\max_{0\le a<n} h\left(a\right)\right) + l + b \cdot \left(64 + 1024 \cdot d \cdot w\right)\right)\right), 0 \right\} \\ &\text{where}\quad v\left(t\right)\left(i\right) = \frac{h\left(i\right)}{\left(1 - t\right) \cdot h\left(i\right) + t} \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} u\left(t\right)\left(i\right) = \frac{n \cdot v\left(t\right)\left(i\right)}{\left(\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} v\left(t\right)\left(j\right)\right)} \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} t = \begin{cases} \operatorname{choose}\left(h\right) & h : \exists t\in \mathbb{R},\;0 \leq t \land \min\left\{ 1 - t, n \cdot \rho - \left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} u\left(t\right)\left(i\right)^{2}\right) \right\} = 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{otherwise} \end{cases} \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} a\left(i\right) = \mu \cdot u\left(t\right)\left(i\right) \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} I = \left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \frac{a\left(i\right)^{2}}{h\left(i\right)}\right) \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} S = \left(\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \frac{1}{h\left(i\right)}\right) \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} U = \left(\max_{0\le i<n} a\left(i\right)\right) \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} M = L \cdot \max\left\{ U \cdot \min\left\{ n, 1 + \sqrt{n \cdot \left(\rho - 1\right)} \right\}, \frac{n \cdot \left(\max_{0\le i<n} \frac{a\left(i\right)}{h\left(i\right)}\right)}{S} \right\} \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} A = \frac{2 \cdot S \cdot M}{I} \\ &\phantom{\text{where}\quad} w = \left\lceil\log_{2}\left(\left\lceil 2 + d + A + \frac{R^{2} + \left(\frac{\sigma \cdot U}{M}\right)^{2}}{\varepsilon} \right\rceil_{+} + 1\right)\right\rceil_{+}\end{aligned}

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Each worker objective fᵢ is convex and differentiable on ℝᵈ. The mean objective F is convex and has an L-Lipschitz gradient. The stated smoothness bound applies to F.

problem_class.label: finite_sum
problem_class.details: F(x) = (1/n)∑ᵢ fᵢ(x), with n ≥ 1 and one hidden component function assigned to each computing worker.
problem_class.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, Params.n, Functions, objective, spec.Instance, and spec.admissible

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A completed evaluation at worker i returns its query point x and a sample gᵢ(x,ξ) with mean ∇fᵢ(x). The sample law may depend on i. The functions, oracle maps, and sample laws are hidden. All Params fields are public, including x₀, d, n, h, l, b, L, μ, ρ, R, σ, and ε.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, Params, spec.publicInput, spec.Instance, and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean, IsStochasticGradient.unbiased. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, ComputeReply and computation

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: Worker i can sample the gradient of its assigned fᵢ at a requested point. Node 0 coordinates communication and has no gradient oracle.

distinctive_assumptions.label: gradient_similarity
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x, (1/n)∑ᵢ‖∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ ρ‖∇F(x)‖², with ρ ≥ 1. This bounds the true worker gradients. At every minimizer of F, all true worker gradients vanish, while stochastic samples may still have positive variance.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every worker and query point, E‖gᵢ(x,ξ)−∇fᵢ(x)‖² ≤ σ², with σ ≥ 0. Each worker uses an i.i.d. sample stream, and the entire streams are independent across workers.

distinctive_assumptions.label: quadratic_growth
distinctive_assumptions.details: Writing X* = argmin F, there is a z ∈ X* with ‖x₀−z‖ ≤ R, and F(x)−F(z) ≥ (μ/2)dist(x,X*)² for every x. The parameters satisfy 0 < μ ≤ L and R ≥ 0. Multiple minimizers are permitted.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The domain and output space are ℝᵈ with the Euclidean norm, for a public natural number d.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Worker i takes a fixed time hᵢ > 0 per evaluation and can have one pending evaluation. Workers and directed star links can operate concurrently, with one message in flight per direction per link. A k-bit payload takes l + b(k + 64) time, including the clock overhead, with l,b ≥ 0.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.valid and spec.admissible. LongTails/Setups/StarNetwork.lean, Network, computation, and communication. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, Time, clockBits, and step

accuracy.label: distance_to_solution
accuracy.details: The designated output node returns a measurable point X at the elapsed-time deadline. Its error is the squared Euclidean distance to the full solution set, dist(X,argmin F)².
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, solutions and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, execute and TimedConvergence

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The squared distance must be integrable and satisfy E[dist(X,argmin F)²] ≤ ε for ε > 0. Expectation is over the product of the algorithm and oracle seed laws. The time budget is fixed by the public parameters, and execution must have finitely many events almost surely through that deadline.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/DistributedMeanStrongGrowth.lean, spec.valid and spec.successful. LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean, law, FiniteEvents, and TimedConvergence

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The setup combines quadratic growth of the mean objective and a relative bound on true worker gradients with persistent sampling noise. It measures time to expected squared solution-set distance on a star with unequal worker speeds, concurrent directed links, message latency, and per-bit charges.
